subject: Uptime discrepancy on 2026-01-09 — maintenance overlap and third-party impact
messages:
From: Jared Lowe <jared.lowe@pulse-med.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-12T08:14:00-08:00
Subject: Uptime discrepancy for 2026-01-09 partial degradation - request for credit

Hi Aisha,

We detected a severe partial degradation affecting our API traffic between 2026-01-09 02:42 - 03:28 UTC (estimated 46 minutes). Our telemetry shows 64% error rate for critical endpoints during that window which impacted patient-facing workflows. We understand Redwood had a maintenance window that morning, but PulseMed did not receive advance notice and our routing shows the failure came from a downstream CDN provider you rely on.

Per section 4.2 of our contract (SLA uptime), we would like Redwood to calculate the downtime credit for the full window. I've attached a short PDF export from our service-monitoring dashboard and a small excerpt of our logs. Please confirm receipt and next steps for an SLA credit.

Attachments: uptime_report_20260109.pdf (PDF, 220 KB); pulsemed_client_logs_excerpt.txt (TXT, 48 KB)

Thanks,
Jared Lowe
Head of Platform
PulseMed
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Lowe <jared.lowe@pulse-med.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai> , Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-12T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Uptime discrepancy for 2026-01-09 partial degradation - request for credit

Hi Jared — thanks for the heads up and for sending the extracts. I've looped in Marissa from Ops and Ben from Accounts so we can triage and respond with a clear apportionment.

Quick notes:
- I can confirm we had a scheduled maintenance slot on 2026-01-09 02:30-03:00 UTC for certificate rotation on a subset of edge nodes; that window was communicated to the account contact on 2025-12-22 and via the console.
- However, your telemetry suggests a longer impact and different symptomology (high error rate rather than brief connection resets). We need to reconcile host-level logs against our CDN partner's incident.

Next steps:
1) Marissa, can you run an initial attribution (maintenance vs third-party) and share a calc sheet we can send to PulseMed?
2) Ben, I'll leave the SLA-credit conversation to you once tech has a recommended apportionment.

I want to keep this tight — can we aim to respond with a proposed credit by EOD Thursday PST?

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior AM, Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-13T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Uptime discrepancy for 2026-01-09 partial degradation - request for credit

Aisha / team — initial findings below after pulling our edge metrics and CDN provider's incident timeline. See attached apportionment_calc.xlsx for line-by-line math.

Summary:
- Our scheduled certificate rotation ran 02:30–02:40 UTC and affected ~8% of traffic routed to a rotating edge pool; that alone would not explain the 64% error rate PulseMed reports.
- At 02:41 UTC the CDN partner (EdgeWave) began reporting elevated packet loss across two POPs that correspond to PulseMed's egress region; EdgeWave's incident extended to ~03:22 UTC.
- Between 02:41–03:22 UTC, our edge retransmits and failover logic engaged; customers on sticky session routing saw higher error rates than those on pooled routes.

Recommended apportionment:
- Assign 12 minutes to Redwood maintenance (02:30–02:42 UTC overlap where maintenance touched PulseMed-affecting pool).
- Assign the remaining 40 minutes to third-party CDN outage (EdgeWave).

Implication per contract:
- Redwood SLOs exclude third-party outages where evidence shows independent failure chain; credit would be applied pro-rata only to the portion attributable to Redwood maintenance (12/52 minutes).

Attachments: apportionment_calc.xlsx (XLSX, 18 KB) — contains timestamps, sample request IDs, and the math.

I'll also flag that EdgeWave has not yet accepted responsibility publicly; we have their incident ticket (EW-5632) and will request their packet capture. If PulseMed prefers, we can run a joint postmortem with EdgeWave and PulseMed ops to get final attribution.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Platform Ops — Redwood Inference
From: Jared Lowe <jared.lowe@pulse-med.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@pulse-med.com
Date: 2026-01-14T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Uptime discrepancy for 2026-01-09 partial degradation - request for credit

Aisha / Marissa — thanks for the quick analysis but PulseMed can't accept a pro-rated credit where the impact was effectively full for our customers. A few points:

1) Our traffic routing shows the population affected across every AZ we use — not a narrow pool. The 64% aggregated error rate is sustained across our health-check surfaces.
2) EdgeWave's ticket number in our correspondence doesn't yet contain packet capture; without that evidence we can't agree to shift liability away from Redwood.

We'd like Redwood to provision the contractual credit for the full 46-minute window while you pursue subrogation with EdgeWave if you believe they are at fault. If you decline that course, please detail the exact calculations and the contract clause you're relying on for the pro-rating.

Forwarded message (excerpt) attached: pulsemed_client_logs_excerpt.txt

-Jared
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Lowe <jared.lowe@pulse-med.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-15T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Uptime discrepancy for 2026-01-09 partial degradation - request for credit

Jared — thanks for the candid feedback and I appreciate the impact to PulseMed's users. I want to propose a path forward that resolves this quickly and preserves the partnership:

1) Goodwill offer: Redwood will apply a full SLA credit equivalent to 46 minutes for January invoice reconciliation while we continue technical attribution with EdgeWave. This is offered as a one-time concession (deal_id PM-2024-0912).
2) Subrogation/forensics: We'll keep pursuing packet captures and a joint postmortem with EdgeWave; if EdgeWave accepts responsibility and makes the creditable finding, we'll either reverse the credit or invoice EdgeWave per our terms.
3) Joint postmortem: propose a call next week with PulseMed ops, Redwood Ops (Marissa's team), and an EdgeWave liaison. I'll include a short DocuSign link to formalize the goodwill arrangement if you want it in writing: https://docusign.com/pm-redwood-offer-20260115

If that sound acceptable, we can have Accounts apply the credit and schedule the call. Aisha — can you confirm PulseMed's preferred time for the postmortem?

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales Lead — Redwood Inference
Attachments: none
